clue.text: Lay down vintage wine in Lancashire

definitions.note: a place-name definition: the clue asks for a town found there

parts.note: to lay down supplies is to stock them, as with a cellar
port is a fortified wine often laid down as a vintage

explanation.surface: Advice to cellar a good bottle of wine somewhere in the north-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCKPORT is a town near Manchester; the part north of the River Mersey lay historically in Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition points to a northern town, one part of which sat historically within the county named.

clue.text: A magnum opus, as far as I'm concerned

parts.note: to, as in 'as far as the gate' or 'to the gate'
the speaker, me, taken as the object form

explanation.surface: Someone declares a book a masterpiece, at least in their personal opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'as far as I'm concerned' reads naturally as 'to me', which is how it splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum opus is a great, usually large, work, and a hefty book is a fitting synonym.

clue.text: It's booked for the diocesan convention

explanation.surface: A church gathering has been reserved in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A section of a book is a natural division of the text, and a cathedral's clergy assembled in council bear the same name.

clue.text: Get expert treatment

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert
a cure is a remedy or course of treatment

explanation.surface: An instruction to seek out a specialist's care.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain or acquire something is a plain synonym for the verb in the definition.

clue.text: Not well done, and that's unusual

explanation.surface: A remark that a steak served bloody is out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked lightly, still red inside, is the opposite of well done, and something seldom seen is uncommon.

clue.text: Paying attention to a job in a GCHQ station

parts.note: listening is paying attention to sounds
a post is a position of employment

explanation.surface: Someone attentive in their work at Britain's intelligence centre.
explanation.walkthrough: GCHQ is Britain's signals intelligence agency, which monitors communications.
explanation.definitionFit: An installation for intercepting enemy signals is just the kind of base a spy agency runs.

clue.text: Lister is into a new development!

definitions.text: Lister is into a new development!

indicators.note: letters given a new development are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A cheer for the Victorian surgeon embracing a fresh advance in medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery, so the whole clue also describes his germ-killing work.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing germs on instruments was the advance associated with the surgeon named.

clue.text: The company's blue-eyed boy has long been popular

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer names something that is so

parts.note: a firm is a business company
a blue-eyed boy is someone's darling, a favourite

explanation.surface: The office pet at the firm has been well liked for years.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steadily liked over a long period is described by the idiom.

clue.text: Get together to study beer and tea blending

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn
a jug of beer, so jug stands for the drink

indicators.note: the letters of tea are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to swot up on mixing ale and a cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: To join or couple is an older sense of the verb, as in bodies joining.

clue.text: Not an upright boast from the proud new parents

definitions.text: Not an upright boast from the proud new parents

parts.words: Not an upright boast from the proud new parents
parts.note: a horizontal piano that is not upright, read also as parents saying their infant is splendid

explanation.surface: Proud parents bragging about their newborn.
explanation.definitionFit: A small horizontal piano is the opposite of an upright, and parents might call their child grand.

clue.text: Retrospective way to acquire a love of porridge

indicators.note: looking back, so the pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Looking back on how one came to like breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospective' turns ST + A + O round to give the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The grain is the main ingredient of the breakfast dish, so the cereal stands for it.

clue.text: Beverage with plenty of body

explanation.surface: A drink described as full-bodied.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark beer is one kind of drink, and a person with plenty of body is portly.

clue.text: Region about to be included by a motoring organisation

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: the AA is Britain's Automobile Association
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A district about to join a drivers' club.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is a British motoring breakdown organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone or district is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Open display of pavement drawing?

parts.note: a pavement lines a street, abbreviated ST
drawing is a form of art

explanation.surface: A public show of chalk pictures on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin or commence is a common meaning of the verb in the definition.

clue.text: A guru disposed to make predictions

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A spiritual teacher inclined to foretell the future.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell or forecast is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: Porter must take rubbish back after New Year's Day

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: January 1st, written JAN and I

indicators.note: the word for rubbish is read backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: A doorman having to haul the trash away once the holiday is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ROT into TOR; I stands for the Roman numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorkeeper or caretaker is also called a porter.

clue.text: Friend to the English queen, no less

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend of the English monarch, nothing less.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as much, in the same measure, is what the adverb means.

clue.text: He's in the services and she's in service

explanation.surface: A man in the military and a woman in domestic work.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior army officer, and a maid-of-all-work in an old household, share the title.

clue.text: Affair giving recurrent trouble to one young lad

indicators.note: running back, so the word for trouble is turned round

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
I is the Roman numeral one
a son is a young lad

explanation.surface: A romance that keeps causing problems for a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret romantic relationship is a sense of the word.

clue.text: Comparatively vulgar utterance from one going to the dogs

indicators.note: spoken out loud, signalling a word that sounds the same

parts.note: coarser means more vulgar

explanation.surface: A ruder remark from someone in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: Coursing is hare-hunting with greyhounds, so a courser is a hunting dog or its handler.
explanation.definitionFit: A hound used in hare-chasing, or its owner, is literally out with the hounds.

clue.text: Longing to get in sugar and pepper

parts.note: cane sugar, so cane stands for sugar
a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A craving to add sweetener and spice.
explanation.definitionFit: The hot red powder is a type of pepper.

clue.text: Kind hearted county people

indicators.note: the heart of the phrase supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Generous rural folk.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort or category is a synonym for kind as a noun.

clue.text: In the woods he would stray wildly

definitions.text: In the woods he would stray wildly

indicators.note: wildly means the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A man in the forest who would roam unrestrained.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland creature of myth, half man and half goat, roamed the forests lustfully.

clue.text: Shock caused by crazy take-over

indicators.note: turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: Surprise at a mad corporate acquisition.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze or astonish someone is what the verb means.

clue.text: Lovely show

explanation.surface: A beautiful exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: Beautiful, as in fair maiden, and an exhibition or fete both carry the word.

clue.text: Before going up it rumbles ominously

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading upwards turns the word backwards

parts.note: ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: Something gives a threatening growl before it rises.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano growls before eruptions.

clue.text: Donkeys I take to the country for slaughter

parts.note: asses are donkeys, here two of them
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Someone drives donkeys across the land to the abattoir.
explanation.definitionFit: A killing, especially a political murder, is a kind of slaughter.

clue.text: He loves to eat marmalade when resident in Ulster

definitions.text: He loves to eat marmalade when resident in Ulster

parts.words: He loves to eat marmalade when resident in Ulster
parts.note: a fruit-jam fan, but really a member of the Protestant Orange Order in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish man with a fondness for orange preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Order is a Protestant fraternal body in Northern Ireland, named after William of Orange.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Orange Order fits the Ulster resident; the marmalade is the joke.
